description: The plot illustrates how loss changes over training time for two methods, “Vanilla” and “SepLLM,” shown as two line series on the same axes. The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale, spanning from 0 to 250,000 seconds with regularly spaced tick labels every 50,000 seconds. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75 with tick labels at 0.05 intervals. The “Vanilla” series is drawn as a purple solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers; it starts near the top of the axis around 2.75 at early training times, then decreases smoothly, reaching about 2.62 near 50,000 s, about 2.57 near 100,000 s, about 2.54 near 150,000 s, and ending around 2.50 at 250,000 s. The “SepLLM” series is drawn as a red solid line with circular markers; it also begins near 2.75 at early times, declines steadily to about 2.61 near 50,000 s, about 2.56 near 100,000 s, about 2.53 near 150,000 s, and ends slightly below 2.50 (around 2.49) by roughly 240,000–250,000 s. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at loss = 2.50, and a green dashed vertical bracketed annotation near the right side spans approximately from 200,000 s to 250,000 s with the label “1.26×.”
